cards.power: Absorb 10 Freedom tokens from all players. You now hold the Monopoly on Violence.
cards.lore: Nietzsche was right. The state is a cold-blooded monster that only exists to maintain its own power.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the Monopoly on Violence. No translation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink wash political cartoon. Subject: monstrous crowned bear with dripping claws. Mood: cold bureaucratic menace.

cards.power: Target player wastes 2 turns arguing with themselves. Nothing changes.
cards.lore: Two identical parties ensure the masses can throw the rascals out without changing the policy.
cards.gradeReason: Makes you perform futile debate. Instantly understood, wickedly funny.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor satire. Subject: two ostriches with blue and red ties, heads in sand sandbox. Mood: absurd futility.

cards.power: Merge your Bank deck with your Government deck. Evade all antitrust attacks.
cards.lore: Mussolini called it corporatism; the postmodern technocrats call it a Public Private Partnership.
cards.gradeReason: Solid satire, needs deck context to perform its full trick.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: weasel in suit fused spine-to-spine with military bulldog. Mood: symbiotic corruption.

cards.power: Play this to cancel any player's action, citing missing paperwork.
cards.lore: Progressive reforms from the ivory tower only serve to disempower the population that pays for them.
cards.gradeReason: You get to BE the bureaucrat. Role is crystal clear and hilarious.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: badger lost in infinite filing cabinet maze. Mood: Kafkaesque helplessness.

cards.power: Transfer 73.85% of target's assets to the player with the most wealth.
cards.lore: Five billion people fall into poverty while the elite double their fortunes. The Ponzi scheme works perfectly.
cards.gradeReason: Works well but feels more like an event card than a character to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk watercolor. Subject: top-hatted frog on steam engine chasing squirrels hoarding acorns. Mood: relentless extraction.

cards.power: You own nothing. Pay 1 token every turn just to keep your cards in your hand.
cards.lore: Trapped in a suffocating corset of subscriptions, streaming, and licenses for things you used to own.
cards.gradeReason: Immediate visceral recognition. The whole table groans and performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: detailed ink. Subject: pigeon wrapped in cables and cords, strangled. Mood: suffocating digital bondage.

cards.power: Discard your hand. It's worthless now anyway.
cards.lore: The normal citizen battles rising taxes and energy costs, left with neither time nor money for a life of dignity.
cards.gradeReason: Worthless now anyway — darkly funny gut-punch that everyone gets instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor. Subject: raccoon throwing coins into monstrous laughing fireplace. Mood: helpless dark comedy.

cards.power: Steal an opponent's resources under the guise of saving the forest.
cards.lore: The 148 largest corporations record 1.8 trillion in profits while lecturing you on your carbon footprint.
cards.gradeReason: Good but asks you to perform a role rather than embody it fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: suited fox with chainsaw and ECO badge felling tree. Mood: hypocritical green-washing menace.

cards.power: Target player forgets their strategy and loses 1 Intelligence token.
cards.lore: Continuous rapid-fire multimedia propaganda melts traditional thought patterns into compliance.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanic, but card is more effect than embodied role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: motion-blur cartoon. Subject: deer stunned by barrage of flying television sets. Mood: overwhelming media assault.

cards.power: Play instantly to turn any random minor action into a global crisis.
cards.lore: As the 1994 US Special Forces manual notes: if the situation is explosive, any historical event can be weaponized as a trigger.
cards.gradeReason: Instant play, instant performance. The table explodes when this drops.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comedy cartoon. Subject: grinning cat with lit match surrounded by dynamite and fireworks. Mood: gleeful crisis manufacture.

cards.power: Force a poorer player to fight your battles. You take the loot, they take the damage.
cards.lore: The rich pay, provide credibility, and the poor are sent to the front lines to die.
cards.gradeReason: Role is instantly legible. A villain card that makes you feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor. Subject: walrus on cushion commanding mouse toward bear trap with scepter. Mood: callous class warfare.

cards.power: Divide an opponent's allied cards. They now attack each other.
cards.lore: Sow discord, disorganization, and subversion. A divided resistance is a defeated resistance.
cards.gradeReason: Solid mechanic, the bilingual name is fun but needs explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychedelic cartoon. Subject: glowing mushroom explosion between two snarling dogs. Mood: manufactured discord, trippy energy.

cards.power: Lock down the board. No one can play cards without a Medical Compliance token.
cards.lore: A bloodthirsty, postmodern rule of terror masked as public health.
cards.gradeReason: COVID lockdown kayfabe crystallized into 8 words. Table gasps, then laughs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark ink wash. Subject: giant syringe wrapped in snake looming over board game landscape. Mood: clinical totalitarian dread.

cards.power: Ignore all ethical rules of the game for the next 3 turns.
cards.lore: Since Robert Koch's colonial camps, the state has never truly stopped treating citizens as guinea pigs.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp lore but power effect is generic; embodiment is vague.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: guinea pig on legal document with stamp, scientists in background. Mood: cold institutional indifference.

cards.power: Target player must play their hand randomly with their eyes closed.
cards.lore: In 1953, the CIA fed thousands of unsuspecting citizens LSD to break the human mind.
cards.gradeReason: Eyes-closed play is the best table mechanic in the deck. Pure chaos-fun.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychedelic explosion. Subject: rabbit head burst with swirling clocks, eyes, neon spirals. Mood: CIA mind-fry carnival.

cards.power: Release a pathogen. All players discard their highest-value card.
cards.lore: For 20 years, the state tested tularemia, typhus, yellow fever, and anthrax on its own.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept, mechanical effect slightly disrupts the flow.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: clinical ink. Subject: vulture in lab coat holding glowing test tube. Mood: detached scientific menace.

cards.power: Slowly drain 1 token from an opponent every turn. You may not tell them why.
cards.lore: For forty years (1932-1972), therapies were intentionally withheld from minorities for study purposes.
cards.gradeReason: May not tell them why — the silence IS the crime. Table goes quiet.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark charcoal. Subject: clawed hand holding syringe in shadow. Mood: silent institutional violence, noir.

cards.power: Paralyze an opponent's deck for 1 turn.
cards.lore: Sarin, mustard gas, and VX tested on 100,000 unwitting soldiers who thought they had bugs under their skin.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is horrifying; power is serviceable but forgettable mechanically.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: monochrome ink. Subject: bulldog in helmet surrounded by gas cloud and flies. Mood: helpless military exposure.

cards.power: Irradiate a zone. Any card played there is instantly destroyed.
cards.lore: Soldiers ordered to drive over radioactive barrels in Hanford, just to see if the trucks offered protection.
cards.gradeReason: Depends on zone mechanics; strong concept, deployment is context-dependent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grim watercolor. Subject: neon-pink mutant pig driving jeep through irradiated wasteland. Mood: tragicomic nuclear sacrifice.

cards.power: Sacrifice a weak card to gain +5 Science Points for the Empire.
cards.lore: Sick children in Oak Ridge blasted with massive radiation, not to cure them, but to see how much astronauts could survive.
cards.gradeReason: Horrifying lore, but the performance depends on a currency not visible elsewhere.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: clinical sci-fi ink. Subject: white mouse in hospital gown attached to ray gun machine. Mood: cold imperial science.

cards.power: Target opponent cannot draw new cards for 2 turns.
cards.lore: From the US to Sweden to Canada, the state legally erased the futures of indigenous and undesirable women.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is devastating; power mechanic feels thin against it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark engraving. Subject: three owls in judge robes against divine light rays. Mood: authoritarian judgment, institutional darkness.

cards.power: Destroy an opponent's population token. Claim it was to lower greenhouse gases.
cards.lore: 166 million UK pounds funded forced sterilization camps in India, justified as fighting climate change.
cards.gradeReason: The roleplay instruction is embedded in the power text. Perfect kayfabe.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: smug sun with thumbs-up next to chained elephant. Mood: environmental PR masking control.

cards.power: Swap one of your weak cards with an opponent's strong card to balance demographics.
cards.lore: A UN strategy from 2000 to compensate for declining birth rates rates through orchestrated migration.
cards.gradeReason: Presents contested far-right framing as fact; neutralizes table rather than sparking play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sepia industrial. Subject: conveyor belt moving animal figures into factory. Mood: dehumanizing systems, controlled displacement.

cards.power: Incite a riot. Both you and your opponent lose 2 cards.
cards.lore: Migrants and citizens are both victims, pushed into violent friction by the faceless supranational empire.
cards.gradeReason: Mutual damage is interesting but blurs who you're embodying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dynamic ink. Subject: two blindfolded badgers about to collide, dynamite between them, invisible hand above. Mood: manufactured conflict.

cards.power: Look at opponent's hand. Discard any card you deem disinformation.
cards.lore: Instead of work camps, we have algorithms silencing dissent before it can even be spoken.
cards.gradeReason: Deem disinformation hands you the totalitarian judge role. Instant theater.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech-noir. Subject: cybernetic octopus smashing printing press with tentacles. Mood: algorithmic censorship, cold digital power.

cards.power: Track an opponent. You can see their cards for the rest of the game.

cards.gradeReason: Persistent surveillance mechanic makes the surveillance STATE visible at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sharp ink. Subject: happy dog with glowing surveillance collar chained to giant eye-phone. Mood: cheerful subjugation.

cards.power: Your vehicles now spy on their drivers. Gain +1 Intel per turn.
cards.lore: By 2027, AI in your own car will permanently monitor you. The 4th industrial revolution is a physical threat.
cards.gradeReason: Good card, loses punch next to the stronger Digital ID Collar concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror cartoon. Subject: panicked cat driving car filled with floating eyeballs. Mood: domestic surveillance nightmare.

cards.power: Skip your turn. You are too busy watching streaming services.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: soft watercolor. Subject: sloth in VR headset drooling on sofa, TV glow. Mood: blissful pacified consumption.

cards.power: Force all players to play the exact same suit/faction this turn.

cards.gradeReason: Strong concept; needs faction system to perform its best trick.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark ink. Subject: line of hamsters in suits marching off cliff edge in lockstep. Mood: conformist mass spectacle.

cards.power: You are exhausted. Maximum hand size reduced to 3.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: hollow-eyed badger clutching coffee cup, steam wisping. Mood: noble exhaustion, quiet defeat.

cards.power: Pay 5 tokens to Big Pharma or lose 2 Health.

cards.gradeReason: Works well but is mechanically familiar; lore is sharper than the mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark watercolor. Subject: rats and mice swarming giant Rx pill bottle amid money piles. Mood: captive market despair.

cards.power: Create a fake defense wall. It shatters the moment it is attacked.
cards.lore: Berlin, Brussels, London, New York, or Beijing: just different facades of the same Potemkin Village.
cards.gradeReason: The reveal moment IS the card's performance. Everyone loves watching it shatter.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: theatrical watercolor. Subject: cardboard castle with prop supports, blue sky backdrop, ruin behind. Mood: staged false security.

cards.power: You control the money supply. Change the cost of any card in play.

cards.gradeReason: The god-mode money power instantly makes you the villain everyone's been looking for.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark ink splash. Subject: black octopus gripping world globe and capitol building simultaneously. Mood: total financial control.

cards.power: Attack an opponent, but gain +5 Public Relations points.
cards.lore: Heads are no longer chopped off, but washed. Postmodern tyranny just hides behind a rainbow pluralism simulation.
cards.gradeReason: PR-positive violence is the deck's sharpest postmodern gag. Gallery-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rainbow watercolor. Subject: grinning hyena in rainbow halo mid-attack, smiling for camera. Mood: cheerful authoritarian PR.

cards.power: Give an opponent 1 token, then steal 5.
cards.lore: Philanthropy is the ultimate mask for extracting global wealth and implementing population control.
cards.gradeReason: The ratio says everything. Simplest mechanic, most devastating takedown.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fairytale ink. Subject: wolf in sheep costume offering lollipop with robotic arm taking wallet behind back. Mood: predatory generosity.

cards.power: Start a proxy war on the board. All other players must discard their hands.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: power ink. Subject: eagle in suit moving chess pieces over board with burning cities. Mood: imperial calculation, collateral indifference.

cards.power: If the ruling player has 10x the wealth of the poorest, trigger a board wipe.
cards.lore: Every empire falls. History teaches us that grotesque excesses of power eventually choke on the power of the many.
cards.gradeReason: Beautiful concept, requires precise game state; can feel anticlimactic if never triggered.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dynamic watercolor. Subject: gold bull charging, market floor crumbling beneath it. Mood: inevitable historical reckoning.

cards.power: All poor players unite their attack power against the wealthiest player.
cards.lore: It is always the same civilizational process. First the bureaucracy, then the police state, then the pitchforks.
cards.gradeReason: Creates instant table alliances. Class war made playable and fun.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: revolutionary ink. Subject: badger, fox, rat, and mouse mob advancing with torches and pitchforks. Mood: inevitable uprising.

cards.power: Reveal all hidden cards. Cancel all active Psy-Ops.
cards.lore: Eventually, even the most conformist statist realizes the politico-media farce has nothing to do with their actual reality.
cards.gradeReason: Thematically perfect endgame card; needs the rest of the deck categories active.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: explosion watercolor. Subject: sheep ripping off VR headset, shattering glass reality behind it. Mood: blinding revelation.

cards.power: The rules of the game slowly break down. Players can ignore 1 rule per turn.
cards.lore: A phase of freedom is followed by institutional decay, corruption, and obscenities.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: decay ink. Subject: classical pillar crumbling with maggots and flies swarming. Mood: institutional entropy, slow rot.

cards.power: Laugh at an attack. Negate all damage and draw a card.
cards.lore: Humor is the universal remedy to wring a fulfilled life out of dark times. A free life.
cards.gradeReason: FrizzleBob manifesto made playable. The deck's emotional north star.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: burst watercolor. Subject: laughing rabbit glowing gold, arrows bouncing off in all directions. Mood: joyful invincibility.

cards.power: You are immune to Propaganda and Psy-Op cards.
cards.lore: Self-determined individuals have the mental capacity to see right through the political-financial Ponzi scheme.
cards.gradeReason: Aspirational immunity is the most desired role at the table. Players race for this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: centered watercolor. Subject: calm meditating turtle in eye of media tornado. Mood: sovereign stillness amid chaos.

cards.power: Change the win condition of the game for all players.
cards.lore: Being against something is easy. We need stories of a freely organized future to inspire the next generation.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-power that rewrites the game itself. Philosophically and mechanically bold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hopeful ink sketch. Subject: beaver with blueprints pointing at treehouse in construction. Mood: constructive utopian vision.

cards.power: You cannot be forced to skip a turn or discard cards by opponent effects.
cards.lore: We fight not just for freedom of speech, but for the preservation of human free will against the Monster.
cards.gradeReason: Solid defense card, but overlaps thematically with Self-Sovereign.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark dramatic ink. Subject: star of light in black void, radiant and defiant. Mood: solitary freedom in darkness.

cards.power: Shuffle these 52 Kayfabe Kards into the main Kult Klub deck. Trust no one.
cards.lore: Because even anarchy needs a layout.
cards.gradeReason: Functional bridge card, cleverly written but it's a utility, not a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kinetic ink. Subject: hand dropping playing cards into blender, cards exploding out. Mood: anarchic system integration.

cards.power: If a rule on these cards contradicts the main game, this card wins. The State always cheats.
cards.lore: Everything is upside down. Doctors destroy health, governments destroy freedom.
cards.gradeReason: Breaks the fourth wall of rules themselves. Meta-satire at its finest.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fire-lit ink. Subject: fox lighting rule book on fire while reading it. Mood: gleeful systemic rule-breaking.

cards.power: [ BLANK SPACE FOR PLAYER TO INVENT THEIR OWN POWER ]
cards.lore: [ BLANK SPACE FOR PLAYER TO WRITE THEIR OWN LORE ]
cards.gradeReason: Radical creative invitation — the most Kayfabizarro thing in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and watercolor stain. Subject: empty white card on field of ink splatter. Mood: open invitation, creative void.

cards.power: Play this card to immediately end the game in a tie. Everyone goes outside.

cards.gradeReason: Everyone goes outside — the best game-ending instruction ever written.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: smoky cartoon. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit bursting from smoke cloud in wide-brimmed hat. Mood: charismatic liberation, mic-drop.

verdict: ShadowPolitics is the deck that FrizzleBob was born to introduce. With 58% G1 cards, nearly every card is a performance instruction in a costume — from the devastating silence of The Syphilis Syringe to the chaotic joy of MK-Mind Melter. The Gumroad ID release confirms this as a polished final product. Weakness: Replacement Migration leans into contested conspiracy framing without the satirical distance that protects the other cards. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 52 cards of political kayfabe from organized crime to bio-security doctrine. For anyone who suspects the game was rigged before they sat down.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob as deranged yellow rabbit atop pile of smashed TVs flanked by badger suits; immediately iconic
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — Ruled by Organized Kayfabe-Krime is perfect punk-political branding with dripping blood-font
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — cover perfectly captures the satirical conspiracy-game energy; nothing misleads
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — the painter-rabbit on TV rubble is genuinely original within the KFB universe
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — strong but niche; reads instantly to insiders, may be opaque to the uninitiated
coverQA.coverNote: Best cover in the ShadowPolitics series. Stay fluffy! as counter-motto to organized kayfabe-krime is a killer tension. QR code on page 13 pointing to CancelThisComic Substack is smart Gumroad integration.

notes: Gumroad ID release of Kayfabizarro_ShadowPolitics_WEB_v1.pdf (previously analyzed). Same 48 cards, same artwork. Differences: QR code on page 13 linking to www.CancelThisComic.SubStack.com/t/Kayfabizarro. Corner RAF-markers vary by page theme: BLODSINN! (p2, systemic cards), KayfaBONGO! (p3-5, economic/bio cards), HUMBUG! (p6-9, experiments/surveillance), KayfaBIZARRO! (p11, uprising cards), Stay fluffy! (p12, resistance/hope cards), KayfaBOGGLE! (p13, meta cards). Page 6 features large background JUSTICE watermark across the state-experiments section — intentional design. Page 13 uses MECHANIC label instead of POWER for cards 45, 46, 48. Replacement Migration contains a typo: birth rates rates (double rates). Card 11 lore ends at die. — iron bear trap is illustration label, not lore text.

urgent: Replacement Migration presents a contested far-right conspiracy theory (Ersatzmigration) as factual UN strategy without satirical framing distance — consider adding FrizzleBob QA note or reframing lore to expose manipulation rather than confirm the premise
Lore typo in Replacement Migration: birth rates rates — double word
quickWins: Digital ID Collar and Surveillance Car share surveillance theme with near-identical power structures — differentiate power effects to reduce redundancy
Standardize MECHANIC vs POWER label across all page 13 cards for rulebook clarity
The Blank Slate artwork (empty white box on ink splatter) is intentionally empty but may look broken in thumbnail/Gumroad preview — consider adding faint FrizzleBob ghost image
